CALL TO ORDER

Co-Chair Tamika Boyce calls the meeting to order at 4:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Rockenbach,
Shuford, Wee, Scott

Commissioners Absent: Brezenoff, Lock, Tan, Topolewski, Lowery-Luyties

Also present: Jennifer Santana, Secretary, Joseph Botelho, Attendee.

Roll call taken by Jennifer Santana.
  • Members Tan, Topolewski, Lock, and Lowery-Luyties were noted as unexcused absent.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-54202  Recommendation to approve submission to U.S. Department of Housing and
  Urban Development (HUD) for non-competitive renewal of Continuum of Care-
  funded projects.

  • Health Department Staff Joseph Botelho provided an update on the timeline
  for FY 2025 CoC Program Notice of Funding (NOFO) actions and legal
  developments.
  • On January 26 HUD disseminated guidance on notification process for
  CoC's not submitting project application or a priority listing to submit projects
  for renewal.
  • HUD reopened the FY 24-25 CoC competition and YHDP Program Grants
  NOFO effective January 9, 2026.

  Page 1 of 3
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 3, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:00 PM

  • Staff recommendation to the board Pathway #1, projects funded in FY 2024
  are not reallocated, replaced, or consolidated, may be eligible for FY 2025
  selection using the FY 2024 submission with written confirmation from
  collaborative applicant. This will be submitted to HUD next week Monday,
  February 9, 2026.
  • Staff will present the board with a project scoring and reallocation and priority
  listing to see where projects will land in the future.

  A motion was made by Member Rockenbach, seconded by Member Shuford,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins,  McFadzen,
  Rockenbach, Shuford, Wee, Scott
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Brezenoff, Lock, Tan, Topolewski, Lowery-Luyties

2.  26-54203  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation approving FY 2025 Continuum
  of Care (CoC) Program Reallocation recommendations.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Martins,  McFadzen,
  Rockenbach, Shuford, Wee, Scott
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Brezenoff, Lock, Tan, Topolewski, Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho provided an update on the
  CoC Program Reallocation Recommendation and next steps. Two types of
  reallocation include involuntary and voluntary. Involuntary reallocation
  standards include performance, utilization, chronic underutilization, spend-
  down, and chronic under spending.
  • Staff are recommending that the Board forgo formal reallocation as part of
  the FY 2025 renewal process based on the following considerations: a
  delayed competition timeline, anticipated federal competition funding
  changes, and the funding risk associated with proposing new projects.
  • As a United Funding Agency (UFA), Long Beach has the authority to shift
  funding outside of the competition. This would help reduce the need for

  short-term NOFO reallocation while preserving flexibility to address
  underperformance through later funding adjustments.
  • The memo that staff plan to submit to HUD was provided in the meeting
  packet. Staff will continue to monitor HUD updates and related litigation or
  court orders and will share updates with the Board as they are released.
  • Members of the Board had questions regarding the current funding in place,
  which staff addressed.
  • A member of the public provided a comment regarding the UFA and who
  designates it.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • Health Department staff member Jennifer Santana announced that board member Daniel
  Brezenoff has voluntarily resigned from his duties. There are now three open board seats.

ADJOURNMENT
